exposure: Gestational age determination at different reference points (obstetric ultrasound assessment at 14 weeks, 20 weeks, ≥20 weeks, or no antenatal ultrasound)
cohort: 2113 births at a perinatal referral center
finding: Pregnancies with gestational age determined by ultrasound at 14 or 20 weeks were associated with a higher chance of non-spontaneous delivery and increased oxytocin use compared to those with later or no ultrasound dating.
mod_finding: The chance of non-spontaneous delivery was higher in pregnancies with 14 weeks ultrasound-based GA (OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.35-1.98) and 20 weeks ultrasound-based GA (OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.31-1.90) when compared to the pregnancies with ≥20 weeks ultrasound-based GA or without any antenatal ultrasound.
